title: Multi-dimensional SDK intake workflow and prioritization matrix for language support, auth patterns, and streaming ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We have a backlog of customer requests for client libraries across languages, varying auth patterns (static tokens, OAuth/OIDC, enterprise SSO rotation), and multiple asks for streaming ergonomics (chunking vs. SSE, resumable streams, backpressure). Current intake is ad-hoc, making prioritization inconsistent for enterprise customers. Goal: Create a repeatable intake workflow and prioritization matrix that balances customer impact, engineering cost, security needs, and platform interoperability so we can make deterministic roadmap decisions for SDK work (hosted + dedicated + private).
scope: Define intake form fields, scoring matrix, review cadence, stakeholder sign-off, and a lightweight gating checklist for security/SSO and streaming ergonomics. Deliverables: intake form template (Confluence + Jira), prioritization matrix spreadsheet, onboarding checklist for engineering, and a one-pager for sales/CS to set customer expectations.
acceptance_criteria: A Confluence intake template exists and is linked from the SDK request page
A prioritization matrix (CSV/Sheet) with weighted criteria covering customer size, revenue, technical complexity, security impact, and alignment to SDK consolidation is published
A documented review cadence and members (PM, Eng owner, Security, Developer Experience) are added to the playbook
Three example customer requests have been triaged using the matrix and outcomes logged
Security gating checklist is validated with Security team and included as a required field in the intake
key_tradeoffs: Routing more requests to a 'shim' mapped to existing SDKs can reduce delivery time but increases long-term maintenance technical debt
Prioritizing breadth of language coverage may dilute engineering focus from hard auth/SSO requirements required by enterprise customers
Making streaming APIs highly ergonomic (resumable, backpressure aware) increases SDK surface and cross-platform testing burden
decisions_to_make: Agree on weights for prioritization criteria and what counts as 'security block' vs 'security advisory'
Define how we treat requests for non-core languages (community contributions vs. internal delivery)
Set SLAs for triage turnaround (initial response within X business days)
stakeholders: Engineering: Marco Li (Client SDKs), Hannah Kim (Runtime integrations)
initial_work_items: Draft intake form on Confluence and embed a short version on the self-serve SDK request page
Create prioritization sheet and run pilot triage on 3 queued requests
Schedule 60-minute cross-functional review to align on weights and gating checklist
Add a lightweight 'streaming ergonomics' section to the intake with sample patterns (SSE, WebSocket, resumable chunking, chunk-signatures)
risks: Over-indexing on high-ARR customers could leave smaller but strategic language communities unsupported
Insufficient engineering estimates lead to repeated scope creep on streaming features
Missing or delayed security review blocks enterprise deliveries
